activities.label: model_1
activities.title: Membrane Selectivity
activities.body: Read the model and note one key rule plus one common mixup.

essentialIdeas: The cell membrane is a selective barrier that lets some substances pass more easily than others.

activities.label: explain_1
activities.title: Explain Membrane Selectivity
activities.body: In one or two sentences, explain how a cell membrane works as a selective barrier.
activities.concept: Cell membrane as a selective barrier
activities.correctAnswer: The cell membrane lets some substances pass more easily than others, so it controls what enters and leaves the cell.
activities.feedback: A complete answer states that the membrane allows some substances through more easily and controls entry and exit. A common gap is saying it lets everything through.

activities.label: repair_1
activities.title: Repair Osmosis Idea
activities.body: Fix your explanation using the model below, then answer again.

essentialIdeas: Osmosis is water moving across a membrane from where water is more available to where it is less available.

activities.label: reexplain_1
activities.title: Explain Osmosis Again
activities.body: Now explain osmosis in your own words without copying the model.
activities.correctAnswer: Osmosis is the movement of water across a membrane from where water is more available to where it is less available.
activities.feedback: A complete answer includes water moving across a membrane and the direction from higher water availability to lower water availability. Do not describe it as movement of the membrane itself.

activities.label: transfer_1
activities.title: Check Osmosis Recognition
activities.body: Choose the best statement about osmosis.
choices: Water moves across a membrane from where water is more available to where it is less available.
Water moves only when a cell uses energy to push it across.
The membrane blocks all water from crossing.
Water moves from where it is less available to where it is more available.
activities.correctAnswer: Water moves across a membrane from where water is more available to where it is less available.
activities.feedback: Osmosis is passive water movement across a membrane, and the direction is from higher water availability to lower water availability.

items.essentialIdea: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, so some substances cross more easily than others.

check.title: Membrane selectivity
check.prompt: How does the cell membrane control what enters and leaves the cell?
check.referenceAnswer: It is selectively permeable, so some substances pass through more easily than others. Different substances cross by different routes or speeds.
check.feedback: The key idea is unequal passage, not a complete block or open gate.

items.essentialIdea: Osmosis is water moving across a membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.

check.title: Water movement in osmosis
check.prompt: What is osmosis across a membrane?
check.referenceAnswer: Osmosis is the movement of water across a membrane from where water is more concentrated to where it is less concentrated.
check.feedback: The direction depends on water concentration, not on the amount of dissolved substance alone.

recognitionCheck.title: Identify osmosis
choices: Water moves across a membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
Glucose moves across a membrane from higher concentration to lower concentration.
A membrane blocks all substances except water.
Water moves only when the cell uses energy.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: Water moves across a membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
recognitionCheck.feedback: Osmosis is passive water movement, not energy-driven transport of any substance.
